1 --- 2 title: How to upgrade to version 16 3 nav_title: Version 16 4 description: Upgrade your Next.js Application from Version 15 to 16. 5 --- 6 7 {/* The content of this doc is shared between the app and pages router. You can use the `Content` component to add content that is specific to the Pages Router. Any shared content should not be wrapped in a component. */} 8 9 ## Upgrading from 15 to 16 10 11 ### Using AI Agents with Next.js DevTools MCP 12 13 If you're using an AI coding assistant that supports the [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io), you can use the **Next.js DevTools MCP** to automate the upgrade process and migration tasks. 14 15 #### Setup 16 17 Add the following configuration to your MCP client, for each coding agent you can read [this section](https://github.com/vercel/next-devtools-mcp#mcp-client-configuration) for configuration details. 18 19 **example:** 20 21 ```json filename=".mcp.json" 22 { 23 "mcpServers": { 24 "next-devtools": { 25 "command": "npx", 26 "args": ["-y", "next-devtools-mcp@latest"] 27 } 28 } 29 } 30 ``` 31 32 For more information, visit the [`next-devtools-mcp`](https://github.com/vercel/next-devtools-mcp) documentation to configure with your MCP client. 33 34 > **Note:** Using `next-devtools-mcp@latest` ensures that your MCP client will always use the latest version of the Next.js DevTools MCP server. 35 36 #### Example Prompts 37 38 Once configured, you can use natural language prompts to upgrade your Next.js app: 39 40 **To upgrade to Next.js 16:** 41 42 Connect to your coding agent and then prompt: 43 44 ```txt 45 Next Devtools, help me upgrade my Next.js app to version 16 46 ``` 47 48 **To migrate to Cache Components (after upgrading to v16):** 49 50 Connect to your coding agent and then prompt: 51 52 ```txt 53 Next Devtools, migrate my Next.js app to cache components 54 ``` 55 56 Learn more in the documentation [here](/docs/app/guides/mcp). 57 58 ### Using the Codemod 59 60 To update to Next.js version 16, you can use the `upgrade` [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160): 61 62 ```bash package="pnpm" 63 pnpm dlx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 64 ``` 65 66 ```bash package="npm" 67 npx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 68 ``` 69 70 ```bash package="yarn" 71 yarn dlx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 72 ``` 73 74 ```bash package="bun" 75 bunx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 76 ``` 77 78 The [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160) is able to: 79 80 - Update `next.config.js` to use the new `turbopack` configuration 81 - Migrate from `next lint` to the ESLint CLI 82 - Migrate from deprecated `middleware` convention to `proxy` 83 - Remove `unstable_` prefix from stabilized APIs 84 - Remove `experimental_ppr` Route Segment Config from pages and layouts 85 86 If you prefer to do it manually, install the latest Next.js and React versions: 87 88 ```bash package="pnpm" 89 pnpm add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 90 ``` 91 92 ```bash package="npm" 93 npm install next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 94 ``` 95 96 ```bash package="yarn" 97 yarn add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 98 ``` 99 100 ```bash package="bun" 101 bun add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 102 ``` 103 104 If you are using TypeScript, ensure you also upgrade `@types/react` and `@types/react-dom` to their latest versions. 105 106 ## Node.js runtime and browser support 107 108 | Requirement | Change / Details | 109 | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | 110 | Node.js 20.9+ | Minimum version now `20.9.0` (LTS); Node.js 18 no longer supported | 111 | TypeScript 5+ | Minimum version now `5.1.0` | 112 | Browsers | Chrome 111+, Edge 111+, Firefox 111+, Safari 16.4+ | 113 114 ## Turbopack by default 115 116 Starting with **Next.js 16**, Turbopack is stable and used by default with `next dev` and `next build` 117 118 Previously you had to enable Turbopack using `--turbopack`, or `--turbo`. 119 120 ```json filename="package.json" 121 { 122 "scripts": { 123 "dev": "next dev --turbopack", 124 "build": "next build --turbopack", 125 "start": "next start" 126 } 127 } 128 ``` 129 130 This is no longer necessary. You can update your `package.json` scripts: 131 132 ```json filename="package.json" 133 { 134 "scripts": { 135 "dev": "next dev", 136 "build": "next build", 137 "start": "next start" 138 } 139 } 140 ``` 141 142 If your project has a [custom `webpack`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/webpack) configuration and you run `next build` (which now uses Turbopack by default), the build will **fail** to prevent misconfiguration issues. 143 144 You have a few different ways to address this: 145 146 - **Use Turbopack anyway:** Run with `next build --turbopack` to build using Turbopack and ignore your `webpack` config. 147 - **Switch to Turbopack fully:** Migrate your `webpack` config to Turbopack-compatible options. 148 - **Keep using Webpack:** Use the `--webpack` flag to opt out of Turbopack and build with Webpack. 149 150 > **Good to know**: If you see failing builds because a `webpack` configuration was found, but you don't define one yourself, it is likely that a plugin is adding a `webpack` option 151 152 ### Opting out of Turbopack 153 154 If you need to continue using Webpack, you can opt out with the `--webpack` flag. For example, to use Turbopack in development but Webpack for production builds: 155 156 ```json filename="package.json" 157 { 158 "scripts": { 159 "dev": "next dev", 160 "build": "next build --webpack", 161 "start": "next start" 162 } 163 } 164 ``` 165 166 We recommend using Turbopack for development and production. Submit a comment to this [thread](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/77721), if you are unable to switch to Turbopack. 167 168 ### Turbopack configuration location 169 170 The `experimental.turbopack` configuration is out of experimental. 171 172 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 173 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 174 175 // Next.js 15 - experimental.turbopack 176 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 177 experimental: { 178 turbopack: { 179 // options 180 }, 181 }, 182 } 183 184 export default nextConfig 185 ``` 186 187 You can use it as a top-level `turbopack` option: 188 189 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 190 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 191 192 // Next.js 16 - turbopack at the top level of nextConfig 193 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 194 turbopack: { 195 // options 196 }, 197 } 198 199 export default nextConfig 200 ``` 201 202 Make sure to review the `Turbopack` configuration [options](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopack). **Next.js 16** introduces various improvements and new options, for example: 203 204 - [Advanced Webpack loader conditions](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopack#advanced-webpack-loader-conditions) 205 - [debugIds](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopack#debug-ids) 206 207 ### Resolve alias fallback 208 209 In some projects, client-side code may import files containing Node.js native modules. This will cause `Module not found: Can't resolve 'fs'` type of errors. 210 211 When this happens, you should refactor your code so that your client-side bundles do not reference these Node.js native modules. 212 213 However, in some cases, this might not be possible. In Webpack the `resolve.fallback` option was typically used to **silence** the error. Turbopack offers a similar option, using `turbopack.resolveAlias`. In this case, tell Turbopack to load an empty module when `fs` is requested for the browser. 214 215 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 216 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 217 218 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 219 turbopack: { 220 resolveAlias: { 221 fs: { 222 browser: './empty.ts', // We recommend to fix code imports before using this method 223 }, 224 }, 225 }, 226 } 227 228 export default nextConfig 229 ``` 230 231 It is preferable to refactor your modules so that client code doesn't ever import from modules using Node.js native modules. 232 233 ### Sass node_modules imports 234 235 Turbopack fully supports importing Sass files from `node_modules`. Note that while Webpack allowed the legacy tilde (`~`) prefix, Turbopack does not support this syntax. 236 237 In Webpack: 238 239 ```scss filename="styles/globals.scss" 240 @import '~bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css'; 241 ``` 242 243 In Turbopack: 244 245 ```scss filename="styles/globals.scss" 246 @import 'bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css'; 247 ``` 248 249 If changing the imports is not possible, you can use `turbopack.resolveAlias`. For example: 250 251 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 252 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 253 254 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 255 turbopack: { 256 resolveAlias: { 257 '~*': '*', 258 }, 259 }, 260 } 261 262 export default nextConfig 263 ``` 264 265 ### Turbopack File System Caching (beta) 266 267 Turbopack now supports filesystem caching in development, storing compiler artifacts on disk between runs for significantly faster compile times across restarts. 268 269 Enable filesystem caching in your configuration: 270 271 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 272 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 273 274 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 275 experimental: { 276 turbopackFileSystemCacheForDev: true, 277 }, 278 } 279 280 export default nextConfig 281 ``` 282 283 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 284 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 285 const nextConfig = { 286 experimental: { 287 turbopackFileSystemCacheForDev: true, 288 }, 289 } 290 291 module.exports = nextConfig 292 ``` 293 294 ## Async Request APIs (Breaking change) 295 296 Version 15 introduced [Async Request APIs](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-15#async-request-apis-breaking-change) as a breaking change, with **temporary** synchronous compatibility. 297 298 Starting with **Next.js 16**, synchronous access is fully removed. These APIs can only be accessed asynchronously. 299 300 - [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) 301 - [`headers`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) 302 - [`draftMode`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/draft-mode) 303 - `params` in [`layout.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout), [`page.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), [`route.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route), [`default.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/default), [`opengraph-image`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/opengraph-image#opengraph-image), [`twitter-image`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/opengraph-image#twitter-image), [`icon`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/app-icons#icon), and [`apple-icon`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/app-icons#apple-icon). 304 - `searchParams` in [`page.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) 305 306 Use the [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#migrate-to-async-dynamic-apis) to migrate to async Request-time APIs. 307 308 ### Migrating types for async Request-time APIs 309 310 To help migrate to async `params` and `searchParams`, you can run [`npx next typegen`](/docs/app/api-reference/cli/next#next-typegen-options) to automatically generate these globally available types helpers: 311 312 - [`PageProps`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#page-props-helper) 313 - [`LayoutProps`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#layout-props-helper) 314 - [`RouteContext`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route#route-context-helper) 315 316 > **Good to know**: `typegen` was introduced in Next.js 15.5 317 318 This simplifies type-safe migration to the new async API pattern, and enables you to update your components with full type safety, for example: 319 320 ```tsx filename="/app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" 321 export default async function Page(props: PageProps<'/blog/[slug]'>) { 322 const { slug } = await props.params 323 const query = await props.searchParams 324 return

Blog Post: {slug}

325 } 326 ``` 327 328 This approach gives you fully type-safe access to `props.params`, including the `slug`, and to `searchParams`, directly within your page. 329 330 ## Async parameters for icon, and open-graph Image (Breaking change) 331 332 > The props passed to the image generating functions in `opengraph-image`, `twitter-image`, `icon`, and `apple-icon`, are now Promises. 333 334 In previous versions, both the `Image` (image generation function), and the `generateImageMetadata` received a `params` object. The `id` returned by `generateImageMetadata` was passed as a string to the image generation function. 335 336 ```js filename="app/shop/[slug]/opengraph-image.js" 337 // Next.js 15 - synchronous params access 338 export function generateImageMetadata({ params }) { 339 const { slug } = params 340 return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }] 341 } 342 343 // Next.js 15 - synchronous params and id access 344 export default function Image({ params, id }) { 345 const slug = params.slug 346 const imageId = id // string 347 // ... 348 } 349 ``` 350 351 Starting with **Next.js 16**, to align with the [Async Request APIs](#async-request-apis-breaking-change) change, the image generating function now receives `params` and `id` as promises. The `generateImageMetadata` function continues to receive synchronous `params`. 352 353 ```js filename="app/shop/[slug]/opengraph-image.js" 354 export async function generateImageMetadata({ params }) { 355 const { slug } = params 356 return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }] 357 } 358 359 // Next.js 16 - asynchronous params and id access 360 export default async function Image({ params, id }) { 361 const { slug } = await params // params now async 362 const imageId = await id // id is now Promise when using generateImageMetadata 363 // ... 364 } 365 ``` 366 367 ## Async `id` parameter for `sitemap` (Breaking change) 368 369 Previously, the `id` values returned from [`generateSitemaps`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-sitemaps) were passed directly to the `sitemap` generating function. 370 371 ```js filename="app/product/sitemap.js" 372 export async function generateSitemaps() { 373 return [{ id: 0 }, { id: 1 }, { id: 2 }, { id: 3 }] 374 } 375 376 // Next.js 15 - synchronous id access 377 export default async function sitemap({ id }) { 378 const start = id * 50000 // id is a number 379 // ... 380 } 381 ``` 382 383 Starting with **Next.js 16**, the `sitemap` generating function now receives `id` as a promise. 384 385 ```js filename="app/product/sitemap.js" 386 export async function generateSitemaps() { 387 return [{ id: 0 }, { id: 1 }, { id: 2 }, { id: 3 }] 388 } 389 390 // Next.js 16 - asynchronous id access 391 export default async function sitemap({ id }) { 392 const resolvedId = await id // id is now Promise 393 const start = Number(resolvedId) * 50000 394 // ... 395 } 396 ``` 397 398 ## React 19.2 399 400 The App Router in **Next.js 16** uses the latest React [Canary release](https://react.dev/blog/2023/05/03/react-canaries), which includes the newly released React 19.2 features and other features being incrementally stabilized. Highlights include: 401 402 - **[View Transitions](https://react.dev/reference/react/ViewTransition)**: Animate elements that update inside a Transition or navigation 403 - **[`useEffectEvent`](https://react.dev/reference/react/useEffectEvent)**: Extract non-reactive logic from Effects into reusable Effect Event functions 404 - **[Activity](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity)**: Render "background activity" by hiding UI with `display: none` while maintaining state and cleaning up Effects 405 406 Learn more in the [React 19.2 announcement](https://react.dev/blog/2025/10/01/react-19-2). 407 408 ## React Compiler Support 409 410 Built-in support for the React Compiler is now stable in **Next.js 16** following the React Compiler's 1.0 release. The React Compiler automatically memoizes components, reducing unnecessary re-renders with zero manual code changes. 411 412 The `reactCompiler` configuration option has been promoted from `experimental` to stable. It is not enabled by default as we continue gathering build performance data across different application types. 413 414 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 415 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 416 417 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 418 reactCompiler: true, 419 } 420 421 export default nextConfig 422 ``` 423 424 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 425 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 426 const nextConfig = { 427 reactCompiler: true, 428 } 429 430 module.exports = nextConfig 431 ``` 432 433 Install the latest version of the React Compiler plugin: 434 435 ```bash package="pnpm" 436 pnpm add -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 437 ``` 438 439 ```bash package="npm" 440 npm install -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 441 ``` 442 443 ```bash package="yarn" 444 yarn add -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 445 ``` 446 447 ```bash package="bun" 448 bun add -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 449 ``` 450 451 > **Good to know:** Expect compile times in development and during builds to be higher when enabling this option as the React Compiler relies on Babel. 452 453 ## Caching APIs 454 455 ### revalidateTag 456 457 [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) now requires a second argument specifying a [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#reference) profile. The single-argument form is deprecated and will produce a TypeScript error. 458 459 ```ts 460 // Before 461 revalidateTag('posts') 462 463 // After 464 revalidateTag('posts', 'max') 465 ``` 466 467 If you need immediate expiration rather than stale-while-revalidate, use [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) in Server Actions instead. 468 469 ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 470 'use server' 471 472 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 473 474 export async function updateArticle(articleId: string) { 475 // Mark article data as stale - article readers see stale data while it revalidates 476 revalidateTag(`article-${articleId}`, 'max') 477 } 478 ``` 479 480 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 481 'use server' 482 483 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 484 485 export async function updateArticle(articleId) { 486 // Mark article data as stale - article readers see stale data while it revalidates 487 revalidateTag(`article-${articleId}`, 'max') 488 } 489 ``` 490 491 Use `revalidateTag` for content where a slight delay in updates is acceptable, such as blog posts, product catalogs, or documentation. Users receive stale content while fresh data loads in the background. 492 493 ### updateTag 494 495 [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) is a new [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data#what-are-server-functions)-only API that provides **read-your-writes** semantics, where a user makes a change and the UI immediately shows the change, rather than stale data. 496 497 It does this by expiring and immediately refreshing data within the same request. 498 499 ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 500 'use server' 501 502 import { updateTag } from 'next/cache' 503 504 export async function updateUserProfile(userId: string, profile: Profile) { 505 await db.users.update(userId, profile) 506 507 // Expire cache and refresh immediately - user sees their changes right away 508 updateTag(`user-${userId}`) 509 } 510 ``` 511 512 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 513 'use server' 514 515 import { updateTag } from 'next/cache' 516 517 export async function updateUserProfile(userId, profile) { 518 await db.users.update(userId, profile) 519 520 // Expire cache and refresh immediately - user sees their changes right away 521 updateTag(`user-${userId}`) 522 } 523 ``` 524 525 This ensures interactive features reflect changes immediately. Perfect for forms, user settings, and any workflow where users expect to see their updates instantly. 526 527 Learn more about when to use `updateTag` or `revalidateTag` [here](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag#when-to-use-updatetag). 528 529 ### refresh 530 531 [`refresh`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/refresh) allows you to refresh the client router from within a Server Action. 532 533 ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 534 'use server' 535 536 import { refresh } from 'next/cache' 537 538 export async function markNotificationAsRead(notificationId: string) { 539 // Update the notification in the database 540 await db.notifications.markAsRead(notificationId) 541 542 // Refresh the notification count displayed in the header 543 refresh() 544 } 545 ``` 546 547 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 548 'use server' 549 550 import { refresh } from 'next/cache' 551 552 export async function markNotificationAsRead(notificationId) { 553 // Update the notification in the database 554 await db.notifications.markAsRead(notificationId) 555 556 // Refresh the notification count displayed in the header 557 refresh() 558 } 559 ``` 560 561 Use it when you need to refresh the client router after performing an action. 562 563 ### cacheLife and cacheTag 564 565 [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) and [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) are now stable. The `unstable_` prefix is no longer needed. 566 567 Wherever you had aliased imports like: 568 569 ```ts 570 import { 571 unstable_cacheLife as cacheLife, 572 unstable_cacheTag as cacheTag, 573 } from 'next/cache' 574 ``` 575 576 You can update your imports to: 577 578 ```ts 579 import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 580 ``` 581 582 ## Enhanced Routing and Navigation 583 584 **Next.js 16** includes a complete overhaul of the routing and navigation system, making page transitions leaner and faster. This optimizes how Next.js prefetches and caches navigation data: 585 586 - **Layout deduplication**: When prefetching multiple URLs with a shared layout, the layout is downloaded once. 587 - **Incremental prefetching**: Next.js only prefetches parts not already in cache, rather than entire pages. 588 589 These changes require **no code modifications** and are designed to improve performance across all apps. 590 591 However, you may see more individual prefetch requests with much lower total transfer sizes. We believe this is the right trade-off for nearly all applications. 592 593 If the increased request count causes issues, please let us know by creating an [issue](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues) or [discussion](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions) item. 594 595 ## Partial Prerendering (PPR) 596 597 **Next.js 16** removes the experimental **Partial Prerendering (PPR)** flag and configuration options, including the route level segment `experimental_ppr`. 598 599 Starting with **Next.js 16**, you can opt into PPR using the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) configuration. 600 601 ```js filename="next.config.js" 602 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 603 const nextConfig = { 604 cacheComponents: true, 605 } 606 607 module.exports = nextConfig 608 ``` 609 610 PPR in **Next.js 16** works differently than in **Next.js 15** canaries. If you are using PPR today, stay in the current Next.js 15 canary you are using. See [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components) for migration patterns. 611 612 ```js filename="next.config.js" 613 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 614 const nextConfig = { 615 // If you are using PPR today 616 // stay in the current Next.js 15 canary 617 experimental: { 618 ppr: true, 619 }, 620 } 621 622 module.exports = nextConfig 623 ``` 624 625 ## `middleware` to `proxy` 626 627 The `middleware` filename is deprecated, and has been renamed to `proxy` to clarify network boundary and routing focus. 628 629 The `edge` runtime is **NOT** supported in `proxy`. The `proxy` runtime is `nodejs`, and it cannot be configured. If you want to continue using the `edge` runtime, keep using `middleware`. We will follow up on a minor release with further `edge` runtime instructions. 630 631 ```bash filename="Terminal" 632 # Rename your middleware file 633 mv middleware.ts proxy.ts 634 # or 635 mv middleware.js proxy.js 636 ``` 637 638 The named export `middleware` is also deprecated. Rename your function to `proxy`. 639 640 ```ts filename="proxy.ts" switcher 641 export function proxy(request: Request) {} 642 ``` 643 644 ```js filename="proxy.js" switcher 645 export function proxy(request) {} 646 ``` 647 648 We recommend changing the function name to `proxy`, even if you are using a default export. 649 650 Configuration flags that contained the `middleware` name are also renamed. For example, `skipMiddlewareUrlNormalize` is now `skipProxyUrlNormalize` 651 652 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 653 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 654 655 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 656 skipProxyUrlNormalize: true, 657 } 658 659 export default nextConfig 660 ``` 661 662 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 663 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 664 const nextConfig = { 665 skipProxyUrlNormalize: true, 666 } 667 668 module.exports = nextConfig 669 ``` 670 671 The version 16 [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160) is able to update these flags too. 672 673 ## `next/image` changes 674 675 ### Local Images with Query Strings (Breaking change) 676 677 Local image sources with query strings now require `images.localPatterns.search` configuration to prevent enumeration attacks. 678 679 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 680 import Image from 'next/image' 681 682 export default function Page() { 683 return 684 } 685 ``` 686 687 If you need to use query strings with local images, add the pattern to your configuration: 688 689 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 690 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 691 692 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 693 images: { 694 localPatterns: [ 695 { 696 pathname: '/assets/**', 697 search: '?v=1', 698 }, 699 ], 700 }, 701 } 702 703 export default nextConfig 704 ``` 705 706 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 707 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 708 const nextConfig = { 709 images: { 710 localPatterns: [ 711 { 712 pathname: '/assets/**', 713 search: '?v=1', 714 }, 715 ], 716 }, 717 } 718 719 module.exports = nextConfig 720 ``` 721 722 ### `minimumCacheTTL` Default (Breaking change) 723 724 The default value for `images.minimumCacheTTL` has changed from `60 seconds` to `4 hours` (14400 seconds). This reduces revalidation cost for images without cache-control headers. 725 726 For some Next.js users, image revalidation was happening frequently, often because the upstream source images missed a `cache-control` header. This caused revalidation to happen every `60` seconds, which increased CPU usage and cost. 727 728 Since most images do not change often, this short interval is not ideal. Setting the default to 4 hours offers a more durable cache by default, while still allowing images to update a few times per day if needed. 729 730 If you need the previous behavior, change `minimumCacheTTL` to a lower value, for example back to `60` seconds: 731 732 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 733 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 734 735 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 736 images: { 737 minimumCacheTTL: 60, 738 }, 739 } 740 741 export default nextConfig 742 ``` 743 744 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 745 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 746 const nextConfig = { 747 images: { 748 minimumCacheTTL: 60, 749 }, 750 } 751 752 module.exports = nextConfig 753 ``` 754 755 ### `imageSizes` Default (Breaking change) 756 757 The value `16` has been removed from the default `images.imageSizes` array. 758 759 We have looked at request analytics and found out that very few projects ever serve 16 pixels width images. Removing this setting reduces the size of the `srcset` attribute shipped to the browser by `next/image`. 760 761 If you need to support 16px images: 762 763 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 764 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 765 766 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 767 images: { 768 imageSizes: [16, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 256, 384], 769 }, 770 } 771 772 export default nextConfig 773 ``` 774 775 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 776 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 777 const nextConfig = { 778 images: { 779 imageSizes: [16, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 256, 384], 780 }, 781 } 782 783 module.exports = nextConfig 784 ``` 785 786 Rather than lack of developer usage, we believe 16 pixels width images have become less common, because `devicePixelRatio: 2` actually fetches a 32px image to prevent blurriness in retina displays. 787 788 ### `qualities` Default (Breaking change) 789 790 The default value for `images.qualities` has changed from allowing all qualities to only `[75]`. 791 792 If you need to support multiple quality levels: 793 794 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 795 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 796 797 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 798 images: { 799 qualities: [50, 75, 100], 800 }, 801 } 802 803 export default nextConfig 804 ``` 805 806 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 807 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 808 const nextConfig = { 809 images: { 810 qualities: [50, 75, 100], 811 }, 812 } 813 814 module.exports = nextConfig 815 ``` 816 817 If you specify a `quality` prop not included in the `image.qualities` array, the quality will be coerced to the closest value in `images.qualities`. For example, given the configuration above, a `quality` prop of 80, is coerced to 75. 818 819 ### Local IP Restriction (Breaking change) 820 821 A new security restriction blocks local IP optimization by default. Set `images.dangerouslyAllowLocalIP` to `true` only for private networks. 822 823 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 824 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 825 826 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 827 images: { 828 dangerouslyAllowLocalIP: true, // Only for private networks 829 }, 830 } 831 832 export default nextConfig 833 ``` 834 835 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 836 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 837 const nextConfig = { 838 images: { 839 dangerouslyAllowLocalIP: true, // Only for private networks 840 }, 841 } 842 843 module.exports = nextConfig 844 ``` 845 846 ### Maximum Redirects (Breaking change) 847 848 The default for `images.maximumRedirects` has changed from unlimited to 3 redirects maximum. 849 850 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 851 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 852 853 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 854 images: { 855 maximumRedirects: 0, // Disable redirects 856 // or 857 maximumRedirects: 5, // Increase for edge cases 858 }, 859 } 860 861 export default nextConfig 862 ``` 863 864 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 865 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 866 const nextConfig = { 867 images: { 868 maximumRedirects: 0, // Disable redirects 869 // or 870 maximumRedirects: 5, // Increase for edge cases 871 }, 872 } 873 874 module.exports = nextConfig 875 ``` 876 877 ### `next/legacy/image` Component (deprecated) 878 879 The `next/legacy/image` component is deprecated. Use `next/image` instead: 880 881 ```tsx 882 // Before 883 import Image from 'next/legacy/image' 884 885 // After 886 import Image from 'next/image' 887 ``` 888 889 ### `images.domains` Configuration (deprecated) 890 891 The `images.domains` config is deprecated. 892 893 ```js filename="next.config.js" 894 // image.domains is deprecated 895 module.exports = { 896 images: { 897 domains: ['example.com'], 898 }, 899 } 900 ``` 901 902 Use `images.remotePatterns` instead for improved security: 903 904 ```js filename="next.config.js" 905 // Use image.remotePatterns instead 906 module.exports = { 907 images: { 908 remotePatterns: [ 909 { 910 protocol: 'https', 911 hostname: 'example.com', 912 }, 913 ], 914 }, 915 } 916 ``` 917 918 ## Concurrent `dev` and `build` 919 920 `next dev` and `next build` now use separate output directories, enabling concurrent execution. The `next dev` command outputs to `.next/dev`. 921 922 Additionally, a lockfile mechanism prevents multiple `next dev` or `next build` instances on the same project. 923 924 Since the development server outputs to `.next/dev`, the [Turbopack tracing command](/docs/app/guides/local-development#turbopack-tracing) should be: 925 926 ```bash package="pnpm" 927 pnpm next internal trace .next/dev/trace-turbopack 928 ``` 929 930 ```bash package="npm" 931 npx next internal trace .next/dev/trace-turbopack 932 ``` 933 934 ```bash package="yarn" 935 yarn next internal trace .next/dev/trace-turbopack 936 ``` 937 938 ```bash package="bun" 939 bunx next internal trace .next/dev/trace-turbopack 940 ``` 941 942 ## Parallel Routes `default.js` requirement 943 944 All [parallel route](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/parallel-routes) slots now require explicit `default.js` files. Builds will fail without them. 945 946 To maintain previous behavior, create a [`default.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/default) file that calls `notFound()` or returns `null`. 947 948 ```tsx filename="app/@modal/default.tsx" 949 import { notFound } from 'next/navigation' 950 951 export default function Default() { 952 notFound() 953 } 954 ``` 955 956 Or return `null`: 957 958 ```tsx filename="app/@modal/default.tsx" 959 export default function Default() { 960 return null 961 } 962 ``` 963 964 ## ESLint Flat Config 965 966 `@next/eslint-plugin-next` now defaults to ESLint Flat Config format, aligning with ESLint v10 which will drop legacy config support. 967 968 Make sure to review our API reference for the [`@next/eslint-plugin-next`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/eslint#setup-eslint) plugin. 969 970 If you're using the legacy `.eslintrc` format, consider migrating to the flat config format. See the [ESLint migration guide](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/configure/migration-guide) for details. 971 972 ## Scroll Behavior Override 973 974 In **previous versions of Next.js**, if you had set `scroll-behavior: smooth` globally on your `` element via CSS, Next.js would override this during SPA route transitions, as follows: 975 976 1. Temporarily set `scroll-behavior` to `auto` 977 2. Perform the navigation (causing instant scroll to top) 978 3. Restore your original `scroll-behavior` value 979 980 This ensured that page navigation always felt snappy and instant, even when you had smooth scrolling enabled for in-page navigation. However, this manipulation could be expensive, especially at the start of every navigation. 981 982 In **Next.js 16**, this behavior has changed. By default, Next.js will **no longer override** your `scroll-behavior` setting during navigation. 983 984 **If you want Next.js to perform this override** (the previous default behavior), add the `data-scroll-behavior="smooth"` attribute to your `` element: 985 986 ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" 987 export default function RootLayout({ children }) { 988 return ( 989 990 {children} 991 992 ) 993 } 994 ``` 995 996 ## Performance Improvements 997 998 Significant performance optimizations for `next dev` and `next start` commands, along with improved terminal output with clearer formatting, better error messages, and improved performance metrics. 999 1000 **Next.js 16** removes the `size` and `First Load JS` metrics from the `next build` output. We found these to be inaccurate in server-driven architectures using React Server Components. Both our Turbopack and Webpack implementations had issues, and disagreed on how to account for Client Components payload. 1001 1002 The most effective way to measure actual route performance is through tools such as [Chrome Lighthouse](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/overview) or Vercel Analytics, which focus on Core Web Vitals and downloaded resource sizes. 1003 1004 ### `next dev` config load 1005 1006 In previous versions the Next config file was loaded twice during development: 1007 1008 - When running the `next dev` command 1009 - When the `next dev` command started the Next.js server 1010 1011 This was inefficient because the `next dev` command doesn't need the config file to start the Next.js server. 1012 1013 A consequence of this change is that, when running `next dev` checking if `process.argv` includes `'dev'`, in your Next.js config file, will return `false`. 1014 1015 > **Good to know**: The `typegen`, and `build` commands, are still visible in `process.argv`. 1016 1017 This is specially important for plugins that trigger side-effects on `next dev`. If that's the case, it might be enough to check if `NODE_ENV` is set to `development`. 1018 1019 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1020 import { startServer } from 'docs-lib/dev-server' 1021 1022 const isDev = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development' 1023 1024 if (isDev) { 1025 startServer() 1026 } 1027 1028 const nextConfig = { 1029 /* Your config options */ 1030 } 1031 1032 module.exports = nextConfig 1033 ``` 1034 1035 Alternatively, use the [`phase`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js#phase) in which the configuration is loaded. 1036 1037 ## Build Adapters API (alpha) 1038 1039 Following the [Build Adapters RFC](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/77740), the first alpha version of the Build Adapters API is now available. 1040 1041 Build Adapters allow you to create custom adapters that hook into the build process, enabling deployment platforms and custom build integrations to modify Next.js configuration or process build output. 1042 1043 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1044 const nextConfig = { 1045 experimental: { 1046 adapterPath: require.resolve('./my-adapter.js'), 1047 }, 1048 } 1049 1050 module.exports = nextConfig 1051 ``` 1052 1053 `adapterPath` was promoted to a stable, top-level option in 16.2.0. See [`adapterPath`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/adapterPath) for the current API reference. 1054 1055 ## Modern Sass API 1056 1057 `sass-loader` has been bumped to v16, which supports [modern Sass syntax](https://sass-lang.com/documentation/js-api/#md:usage) and new features. 1058 1059 ## Removals 1060 1061 These features were previously deprecated and are now removed: 1062 1063 ### AMP Support 1064 1065 AMP adoption has declined significantly, and maintaining this feature adds complexity to the framework. All AMP APIs and configurations have been removed: 1066 1067 - `amp` configuration from your Next config file 1068 - `next/amp` hook imports and usage (`useAmp`) 1069 1070 ```tsx 1071 // Removed 1072 import { useAmp } from 'next/amp' 1073 1074 // Removed 1075 export const config = { amp: true } 1076 ``` 1077 1078 - `export const config = { amp: true }` from pages 1079 1080 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1081 const nextConfig = { 1082 // Removed 1083 amp: { 1084 canonicalBase: 'https://example.com', 1085 }, 1086 } 1087 1088 export default nextConfig 1089 ``` 1090 1091 Evaluate if AMP is still necessary for your use case. Most performance benefits can now be achieved through Next.js's built-in optimizations and modern web standards. 1092 1093 ### `next lint` Command 1094 1095 The `next lint` command has been removed. Use Biome or ESLint directly. `next build` no longer runs linting. 1096 1097 A codemod is available to automate migration: 1098 1099 ```bash package="pnpm" 1100 pnpm dlx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1101 ``` 1102 1103 ```bash package="npm" 1104 npx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1105 ``` 1106 1107 ```bash package="yarn" 1108 yarn dlx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1109 ``` 1110 1111 ```bash package="bun" 1112 bunx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1113 ``` 1114 1115 The `eslint` option in the Next.js config file is also removed. 1116 1117 ```js filename="next.config.mjs" 1118 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 1119 const nextConfig = { 1120 // No longer supported 1121 // eslint: {}, 1122 } 1123 1124 export default nextConfig 1125 ``` 1126 1127 ### Runtime Configuration 1128 1129 `serverRuntimeConfig` and `publicRuntimeConfig` have been removed. Use environment variables instead. 1130 1131 **Before (Next.js 15):** 1132 1133 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1134 module.exports = { 1135 serverRuntimeConfig: { 1136 dbUrl: process.env.DATABASE_URL, 1137 }, 1138 publicRuntimeConfig: { 1139 apiUrl: '/api', 1140 }, 1141 } 1142 ``` 1143 1144 ```tsx filename="pages/index.tsx" 1145 import getConfig from 'next/config' 1146 1147 export default function Page() { 1148 const { publicRuntimeConfig } = getConfig() 1149 return

API URL: {publicRuntimeConfig.apiUrl}

1150 } 1151 ``` 1152 1153 **After (Next.js 16):** 1154 1155 For server-only values, access environment variables directly in Server Components: 1156 1157 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 1158 async function fetchData() { 1159 const dbUrl = process.env.DATABASE_URL 1160 // Use for server-side operations only 1161 return await db.query(dbUrl, 'SELECT * FROM users') 1162 } 1163 1164 export default async function Page() { 1165 const data = await fetchData() 1166 return
{/* render data */}
1167 } 1168 ``` 1169 1170 > **Good to know**: Use the [taint API](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/taint) to prevent accidentally passing sensitive server values to Client Components. 1171 1172 For client-accessible values, use the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix: 1173 1174 ```bash filename=".env.local" 1175 NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL="/api" 1176 ``` 1177 1178 ```tsx filename="app/components/client-component.tsx" 1179 'use client' 1180 1181 export default function ClientComponent() { 1182 const apiUrl = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL 1183 return

API URL: {apiUrl}

1184 } 1185 ``` 1186 1187 To ensure environment variables are read at runtime (not bundled at build time), use the [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection) function before reading from `process.env`: 1188 1189 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 1190 import { connection } from 'next/server' 1191 1192 export default async function Page() { 1193 await connection() 1194 const config = process.env.RUNTIME_CONFIG 1195 return

{config}

1196 } 1197 ``` 1198 1199 Learn more about [environment variables](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables). 1200 1201 ### `devIndicators` Options 1202 1203 The following options have been removed from [`devIndicators`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/devIndicators): 1204 1205 - `appIsrStatus` 1206 - `buildActivity` 1207 - `buildActivityPosition` 1208 1209 The indicator itself remains available. 1210 1211 ### `experimental.dynamicIO` and `experimental.useCache` 1212 1213 The `experimental.dynamicIO` and `experimental.useCache` flags are deprecated. Use top-level [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) instead. 1214 1215 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1216 // Before: experimental.useCache 1217 module.exports = { 1218 experimental: { 1219 useCache: true, 1220 }, 1221 } 1222 ``` 1223 1224 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1225 // Before: experimental.dynamicIO 1226 module.exports = { 1227 experimental: { 1228 dynamicIO: true, 1229 }, 1230 } 1231 ``` 1232 1233 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 1234 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 1235 1236 // After 1237 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 1238 cacheComponents: true, 1239 } 1240 1241 export default nextConfig 1242 ``` 1243 1244 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 1245 // After 1246 module.exports = { 1247 cacheComponents: true, 1248 } 1249 ``` 1250 1251 For more on Cache Components, see [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components). 1252 1253 ### `unstable_rootParams` 1254 1255 The `unstable_rootParams` function has been removed. We are working on an alternative API that we will ship in an upcoming minor release. 1256
